summary.headline: Azad Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record Rs 187.8 crore (+31.6% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 37.5%, while PAT grew only 6.6% in H1 on investment-phase costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue reached a record Rs 187.8 crore, up 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 70.4 crore (37.5% margin vs 36% a year ago). H1 revenue grew 29.3% to Rs 358 crore, ahead of the 25% guidance. Profit after tax was Rs 30.8 crore in Q2 (16.4% margin), and H1 PAT rose 6.6% to Rs 67.2 crore because of lower treasury income, higher depreciation, finance costs and employee costs. Management said all six customer-dedicated facilities are now commissioned, throughput begins in Q3 FY27, and revenue ramps from Q4 FY27 with full ramp-up by H1 FY28, targeting an annual revenue run rate above Rs 1,300 crore by end FY28.

segments.name: Energy, oil and gas
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 28.5% to Rs 219 crore, about 81% of revenue; Q2 revenue Rs 152 crore (+30% YoY). Dedicated oil and gas facility adds growth from Q4 FY27; contract with a key customer extended to 2030.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 28.3% to Rs 60.4 crore (about 17% of revenue); Q2 revenue Rs 31.7 crore (+31.6% YoY). Delta qualifications under way with Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and Safran for aero engine airfoils; first GTRE turbojet engine delivered.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: H1 domestic revenue more than 2.5x to Rs 43 crore, now 12% of business (from 6%), helped by indigenisation work with BHEL; BHEL long-term rate contract worth about Rs 52.6 crore for gas turbine airfoils.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share was 88% of Q2 revenue; management expects it to stay above 85%.

guidance_outlook: Throughput from new capacity begins in Q3 FY27; revenue ramps from Q4 FY27 and all plants fully ramped by H1 FY28.
Installed capacity supports annual revenue run rate above Rs 1,300 crore by end FY28, more than double FY26 revenue; management said this is a conservative floor and may be exceeded.
Long-term annual growth guidance of over 25% reiterated.
Management expects EBITDA margin to reach its long-term guidance in the coming quarter or so; indirect costs to stay near 7-8% of revenue.
Cash generation expected from Q4 FY27 as inventory converts to receivables; Q1 FY28 described as comfortable.
Energy share of revenue expected to fall to about 55-60% by FY30 as aerospace and defence grow.
capex_capacity: All six customer-dedicated facilities commissioned in Tumkur (about 44,800 sq m in total) for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, GE, Siemens Energy and Baker Hughes; two new facilities inaugurated in September 2026.

Rs 251 crore of new assets capitalised in H1 FY27; Rs 139.3 crore capex in H1 funded by Rs 80.8 crore QIP proceeds, Rs 28.6 crore term loan and internal funds; gross fixed asset base including capital WIP at Rs 1,169 crore.
Of Rs 700 crore QIP proceeds, Rs 621.8 crore used; Rs 78.2 crore remaining earmarked for the capex plan.
Manganpett phase two land is ready; Tumkur phase one fully utilised with one or two buildings still available.
Aerospace customers seeking dedicated facilities on a similar model; no new capex plan announced beyond FY29 yet, to be shared as customer qualifications progress.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strengthening across energy, oil and gas, aerospace and defence; the question is conversion of capacity into revenue.
Management said the order book is a rolling set of customer contracts covering 5-7 years of demand, currently close to Rs 6,000 crore, rather than a conventional backlog.
Wallet share with existing customers is under 2% (single digit), leaving room for growth.
One OEM agreed to a 50% advance against purchase orders, expected to bring about USD 4.5 million; the discount given was about 1%.
Bill discounting lines in place with ICICI Bank and DBS Bank, usable from Q4 FY27 to cut debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new facilities move from development to production, and when will revenue accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buildings, capex and most machines are in place and spindles are running; throughput started with a two to three week delay, with supplies from end Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capacity build-out sufficient to reach Rs 1,800-1,900 crore potential, and will revenue exceed Rs 1,300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 1,300 crore plus run rate is the minimum guidance and the current capacity view has moved beyond it; an updated range may come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a step-up in order backlog and what are the cash-flow timing and peak cash burn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is contracted demand rather than backlog; cash inflows expected from Q4 FY27, with Q1 FY28 comfortable, and bill discounting to help.

qa_highlights.question: How will labour scale and automation plans as revenue grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manpower costs are front-loaded ahead of revenue and expected to fall within one to two quarters as throughput arrives; lean manufacturing and automation targeted to reduce manpower dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Replacement cycle and aftermarket exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot see whether parts go to aftermarket or new builds; gas turbine cold-section parts replaced every 10-12 years and steam/thermal parts every 16-18 years. Hot-section answer deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Discount given to customers for advances and the drop in other operating income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount is about 1% only; it did not directly address the other operating income question, which was to be taken offline.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory of Rs 425 crore (Rs 72 crore in WIP for new lines pending customer approval) and receivables of Rs 402 crore; operating cash flow still negative in H1.
Delta qualification timing for new facilities; revenue from the new lines depends on customer approvals and any slippage (already two to three weeks on throughput).

Profit lag: PAT growth of 6.6% in H1 with rising depreciation (Rs 21.8 crore/quarter), finance costs (Rs 12.2 crore/quarter) and employee costs (Rs 50.3 crore/quarter); other income falling as treasury cash is deployed.
Concentration: energy and oil and gas still about 81% of revenue; aerospace qualifications (Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney, Safran) and GTRE engine testing still pending.
Management to update next quarter on the capacity range, the aerospace dedicated facility model, first aero-engine airfoil qualification batch, and capex plans beyond FY29.
key_quotes: For Azad, the question is not demand. It's how quickly we convert capacity into revenue. And that is a key message for this quarter.
We do not engage in speculative expansion.
The throughput for the business begins improving in H2 FY 27.
So this is the bare minimum we have said key. This will cross it definitely will grow to the level.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity readiness, saying the foundation is complete and throughput has started. Cautious and evasive on specifics: they declined to size the next capacity phase beyond FY29, would not give an updated capacity range, called the Rs 6,000 crore figure contracted demand rather than backlog, and did not directly answer the other operating income question.

growth.why: Management reiterates long-term growth of over 25% and guides an annual revenue run-rate above Rs 1,300 crore by end FY28 (more than double FY26), backed by six commissioned dedicated facilities with throughput from Q3 FY27, full ramp by H1 FY28, and a rolling order book of about Rs 6,000 crore; the timeline and capacity are concrete but the order book is described as contract-based 5-7 year deman
